clue.text: One who conducted reel for part of orchestra

parts.note: Sir Henry Wood, the English conductor who founded the Proms concerts in London
to reel in a fishing line is to wind it round a spool

explanation.surface: A former conductor danced a reel with one section of his orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reel' looks like the dance but is a verb meaning to turn a line in; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The section of instruments played by blowing, such as flutes, oboes and clarinets, is an orchestral section.

clue.text: Skill of a speaker or a politician

parts.note: taken as written
a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A question of whether a talent belongs to a public speaker or a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent public speaking is the art of rhetoric, a talent of those who address crowds.

clue.text: A monstrous female in transvestite clothing? No point!'

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex, as worn by a cross-dressing performer
O, the round figure zero, stands for no or nothing
a ness is a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea, as in Dungeness

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman dressed in drag is told her outfit has no point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between definition and wordplay. NESS, a headland, appears in English place names such as Dungeness and Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: A female dragon is a fearsome she-monster, and by extension a formidable, frightening woman.

parts.note: someone contributing to a project is in on it
a grid is a network of lines, or of power cables

explanation.surface: A young woman helps to build a network.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian female given name, borne by the actress Bergman, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Attack on King spotted arrest follows

indicators.note: follows places the word for arrest after the word for spotted

parts.note: spotted means found or noticed
to arrest movement is to check, halt or stop it

explanation.surface: Police spot a suspect and an arrest follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital K hints at chess. The dash in the printed clue is punctuation only.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, moving one piece to unmask a line of attack from another onto the enemy monarch is this kind of threat.

clue.text: Mulled wine set beside the King

definitions.meaning: an old English hot drink of port spiced with oranges and cloves
in chess, the piece placed next to the king at the start of the game, on the side away from the queen

explanation.surface: Hot spiced wine is served next to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by a hot spiced port drink and the diagonally moving chess piece positioned beside the monarch.

clue.text: Players I judge for criminal activity

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, or players
to try a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: A musician says the band's members and he will judge a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbery by outlaws, especially on the highway, is this sort of lawless activity.

parts.note: read as one bag that alone is roomy enough to take every item you pack, a single case that suffices

explanation.definitionFit: A large soft travelling bag for miscellaneous belongings is named for being able to contain everything.

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of the author's name take a new order

explanation.surface: A building feature appears in a book by J. B. Priestley.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright, which makes 'novel' look like a noun. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of columns surrounding a courtyard or building is a classical architectural feature.

indicators.note: concealed tells us the single letter a is hidden inside the word for accident

parts.note: prang is British slang for a minor crash or bump in a car

explanation.surface: Someone has an accident while carrying a concealed weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'concealed' looks like a description of the weapon but puts A inside PRANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy Malay chopping knife, like a machete, serves as both tool and weapon.

definitions.meaning: strange or peculiar, out of the ordinary
in grammar, the number form referring to one thing only, as opposed to plural

explanation.surface: A number that is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both peculiar and, in grammar, the one-item form of a noun as against the plural.

clue.text: Russian who scored nothing in defeat by the French

parts.note: Alexander Borodin, the Russian composer of Prince Igor, scored music
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A Russian footballer fails to score as his side loses to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' suggests sport but means writing music; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's army beat the Russians in this bloody 1812 battle west of Moscow.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to deal out cards is to share them among the players

explanation.surface: A person of lofty morals holds stock in a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards of perfection one aims to live by are lofty moral principles.

clue.text: Used 27 to write in fourth class?

parts.note: type means a class or kind
D is the fourth letter, so grade D is the fourth class after A, B and C

explanation.surface: Someone tapped away at a keyboard in a fourth-class railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer at 27 across, KEYBOARD. 'in' is a link word, and the question mark flags 'fourth class' as a whimsical grade-D kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing text by striking keys is the work of a typist, so this is the past tense of that action.

definitions.meaning: of the highest rank or quality, elite
the supersonic airliner cruised far higher than ordinary jets, so a trip on it was literally a lofty air journey

explanation.surface: Premium passengers on the supersonic airliner were treated to excellent service.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the highest grade of anything, and punningly describes a journey made at great altitude.

indicators.note: fiddled means tampered with or rigged, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter is cheated by unscrupulous art dealers.
explanation.definitionFit: The English illustrator Aubrey, famed for black-and-white drawings in the 1890s, was an artist.

indicators.note: reformed means formed afresh, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the plural possessive gives its letters, the apostrophe being no letter

explanation.surface: Romanians' republic has been reformed after a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny state enclosed by Italy is one of the world's oldest republics.

definitions.meaning: to grow rapidly in size or number, like something rolling downhill and gathering mass
a frozen projectile thrown in a winter play fight, read apart from the historical Cold War

explanation.surface: Missiles multiplied during the Cold War arms race.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase rapidly is the verb sense, and a pressed lump of snow is the icy projectile in a mock fight.

clue.text: Ineffective player coach takes on, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a team member who contributes nothing and is carried by the others
a bus or coach picks up travellers; perhaps marks this as one example

explanation.surface: A team coach signs a weak player, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A teammate who is carried resembles a traveller who rides rather than drives, and a coach picks up travellers.

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Remaining somewhere awfully dark and dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: From the River Styx of the Greek underworld, the word means hellishly murky.

definitions.meaning: in card games such as bridge, the jack is one of the honour cards
an old word for a rogue or dishonest man, one of a band of thieves

explanation.surface: The proverb about honour among thieves, posed as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the proverb 'honour among thieves'; in bridge, the ace, king, queen, jack and ten are the honours.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack in a pack of cards and an old-fashioned scoundrel share this name.

clue.text: One calls for face-saving device to conceal it

indicators.note: to conceal means to hide within, so the word it goes inside the guard's letters

parts.note: a visor is a hinged guard on a helmet that protects the face

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a device that saves face and helps hide something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-saving' usually means preserving dignity; here it is literal protection for the face. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who calls on someone, paying a call at a house, is a guest or caller.

clue.text: Immerse yourself, but not totally, in the river

indicators.note: not totally says only part of the words immerse yourself is used, a stretch from within them

explanation.surface: Advice to bathe partly in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mersey is the river of Liverpool in north-west England. 'but' and 'in' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the river flowing past Liverpool into the Irish Sea.

definitions.meaning: stayed hidden or out of sight, avoiding attention, in the past tense
to strike down or overthrow an opponent

explanation.surface: Someone stayed silent after a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the past of lie low, meaning stayed hidden, and also a verb meaning to fell an enemy.

clue.text: In church, clergyman silly to create deep split

indicators.note: In at the head of the clue puts the clergyman and the fool inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
Rev, short for reverend, is a clergyman
a silly is a foolish person, an ass

explanation.surface: A foolish vicar causes a schism in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to create' is a link word; 'split' suggests a church schism but means a crack in ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep crack in a glacier or ice sheet is this kind of fissure.

clue.text: Slide, as seen, possibly, on front of glacier

definitions.text: Slide, as seen, possibly, on front of glacier

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the reworked letters after the glacier's opening letter
front of picks out the opening letter of the word glacier
possibly signals that the words slide and as may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mountaineer slides down the snout of a glacier.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: G, the first letter of glacier, then LISSADE from rearranging SLIDE AS, signalled by 'possibly'. 'seen' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A controlled slide down a snow slope on one's boots, used by mountaineers, is exactly the action described.

definitions.meaning: moves or alters position, as a verb
simple loose dresses or chemises, plural garments

explanation.surface: Someone changes their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter or move is the verb sense, and loose straight dresses are the garments.

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole run of letters is read in reverse

parts.note: isn't written out in full is the two words is not

explanation.surface: A small organ has been left behind and is not returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LISNOT, from L plus IS NOT, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two small masses of lymph tissue at the back of the throat is a minor organ.

clue.text: Part of computer showing crucial table

parts.note: key means crucial or vital
a board is a table, as in a festive board

explanation.surface: A computer component sits on an important table.
explanation.definitionFit: The bank of lettered keys for input is a component of a desktop computer.
